title: Microsoft Purview: row-level counting of exact data match (EDM) matches
summary: The counting modes, licensing and roadmap details are supported, and the briefing correctly leaves the default and existing-classifier behaviour unresolved. Minor corrections should acknowledge conflicting Microsoft guidance on navigation, permissions and auto-labelling, complete the wizard heading, and cite the broader policy-count evidence.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: impact
claims.claim: Match counts can determine whether policy conditions are met, supplying the premise for the briefing's threshold-risk analysis.
claims.quote: A satisfied pattern match returns a count and confidence level, which you can use in the conditions in your policy. When you add a condition for detecting a sensitive information type to a policy, you can edit the count and confidence level as shown in the following diagram.
claims.fix: Add https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/sit-create-a-custom-sensitive-information-type-in-scc-powershell to sources for the general policy-count premise. The already-cited EDM testing page additionally confirms that DLP or auto-labeling rules requiring multiple matches might not trigger.

claims.where: Why it matters; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Learn advises choosing Primary Match-level Counting for a detailed view of all sensitive matches.
claims.quote: Primary Match-level Counting: Counts each matching combination of primary and supporting elements separately—even within the same row. Choose this if you want a detailed view of all sensitive matches.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Learn advises Row-level Counting when the question is how many unique sensitive records there are rather than how many elements matched.
claims.quote: Row-level Counting: Counts each row only once, even if multiple elements match in it. Use this when you care about how many unique records (rows) are sensitive, not how many elements matched.

claims.quote: Searched: Purview EDM unique counting permissions identity change existing classifiers rollout. Read the creation guide's Permissions and counting sections, the EDM overview, and Purview permissions search excerpts; none states a counting-mode-specific identity or permission change.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Scope
claims.claim: Schemas created in the classic experience are not viewable or manageable in the new experience.
claims.quote: All schemas that are created using the classic experience or uploaded as an XML file using PowerShell aren't viewable or manageable in the new experience.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Scope

claims.where: Scope
claims.claim: The new experience creates one schema per EDM SIT.
claims.quote: Each time you create an EDM SIT using the new experience, a new schema is created. This results in a 1:1 mapping between EDM schema and EDM SIT.

claims.where: Scope
claims.claim: The new experience limits creation and management to 10 EDM SITs.
claims.quote: Because the new experience doesn't support mapping multiple SITs to the same schema, you're limited to creating and managing 10 EDM SITs.
